title: The Late Parish
premise: True-crime podcaster Casper Eriksen receives two letters about the 40-year-old disappearance of parish organist Lila Voss: one from a dying man confessing to her murder, one unsigned, claiming Lila is alive and will appear at the parish's anniversary dinner. Investigating the remote coastal town of Halloway's End, Casper uncovers a web of inheritance fraud, a church trust stolen from Lila's family, and witnesses bound by decades of loyalty to a beloved patriarch. The climax comes at the anniversary dinner, where Casper exposes the patriarch's son — the real killer — and the 'dead' witness, Lila's sister living hidden under a new name, finally testifies, choosing truth over the loyalty that silenced her for forty years.
about_author: Emrys Almeida is the pen name of a former parish archivist who spent fifteen years cataloguing the secrets of small-town church records before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about the lies communities tell themselves to stay whole.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: POV Casper. On a rain-slicked morning, Casper opens twin letters about the Lila Voss case: a deathbed confession signed by Aldous Merrick, and an unsigned note insisting Lila lives. The handwriting, Casper realizes with a chill, is identical. Emotional beat: the thrill of a lifetime story curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Parish That Forgot
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper arrives in Halloway's End, a town polished for its anniversary celebrations. Locals offer warm smiles and colder answers; the Voss name draws visible flinches. Emotional beat: the uncanny feeling of being welcomed and warned at once.

chapters.title: A Confession Worth Dying For
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper visits Aldous Merrick in a hospice, expecting a monster. Instead he finds a man terrified, recanting even as he signs a statement — 'They'll know I talked.' Emotional beat: pity warring with suspicion; the confession feels rehearsed.

chapters.title: The Organist's Empty Loft
chapters.summary: POV Casper, with flashback fragments. Casper breaks into Lila's preserved loft and finds her music journals, pages torn from 1985. A neighbor's dog barks; someone was watching the house. Emotional beat: intimacy with a ghost, and the first sense of being hunted.

chapters.title: Sons of the Vestry
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper interviews Julian Merrick, Aldous's son and the parish's charming chairman, mid-fundraiser. Julian is magnetic, generous, and deflects with surgical grace. Emotional beat: admiration turning to unease — too much charm, too many rehearsed griefs.

chapters.title: The Trust Nobody Questions
chapters.summary: POV Casper, aided by amateur historian Dot Fenwick. Dot reveals the Voss family trust was folded into the parish endowment in 1986, enriching the Merrick dynasty. Emotional beat: righteous anger — the motive was money, laundered through piety.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Casper. A storm exposes a rusted lockbox on the tideline containing Lila's locket and a woman's shoe. The coroner from 1985 ruled no body was ever found. Emotional beat: hope rekindling — if there's no body, the second letter might be true.

chapters.title: Forty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The town's old constable, now senile, murmurs fragments: 'the sister saw,' 'we kept her safe.' Casper learns Lila had a sister, Maren, listed as dead in 1987. Emotional beat: the vertigo of a second ghost.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guest List
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Julian announces the anniversary dinner will honor 'all our lost souls' — including Lila. Casper notices the guest list includes a woman named Mara Venn, a name that doesn't check out. Emotional beat: the trap and the invitation are the same thing.

chapters.title: Dot's Archive Fire
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Dot's cottage burns the night after she copies the trust ledgers. She survives, shaken, whispering that someone called her by her childhood nickname — something only a local would know. Emotional beat: fear made personal; the past is fighting back.

chapters.title: The Letter Writer's Voice
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper traces the unsigned letter to stationery from a convent two counties away. A retired nun admits a woman has lived there for decades, sending one letter a year — always unmailed, always burned. This year, she mailed it. Emotional beat: a witness choosing, at last, to be heard.

chapters.title: Mara Venn
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper finds Mara Venn — older, wary, unmistakably Lila's sister Maren. She neither confirms nor denies; she only says, 'If you say her name at that dinner, people will die.' Emotional beat: the witness is real, alive, and more afraid of loyalty than of him.

chapters.title: What Maren Saw
chapters.summary: POV Maren. Flashback to 1985: teenage Maren watched from the organ loft as her sister argued with young Julian over the trust — and saw him follow her toward the cliff path. She never saw a body; she saw the town decide. Emotional beat: guilt of the survivor who chose silence to survive.

chapters.title: Aldous Dies
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Hours before his sworn statement can be notarized, Aldous Merrick dies — quietly, 'of his illness.' His nurse mentions a visitor with a parish car sticker. Emotional beat: grief and fury; the confession is now a corpse.

chapters.title: The Podcast Goes Up
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper releases an episode naming the trust fraud and Julian's presence at the cliff path. Downloads explode; so does the town's hostility. His car is keyed, his motel room searched. Emotional beat: isolation — the truth has made him the town's enemy.

chapters.title: Julian's Version
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Julian invites Casper to dinner, all candor and charm: yes, he argued with Lila; yes, his father confessed; but Aldous confessed to protect him from a smaller sin — an affair, not a murder. Emotional beat: doubt — the story almost fits, and Casper hates how much he wants it to.

chapters.title: The Second Shoe
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Forensics on the lockbox shoe match a pair Lila owned; inside the heel, a microfilm of the original trust deed — stolen from the Merricks, hidden as insurance. Lila wasn't fleeing; she was bargaining. Emotional beat: the victim reassembling herself into a player, not a prize.

chapters.title: Where the Bells Don't Ring
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper finds the parish's sealed crypt records: a coffin from 1985, exhumed and reburied empty two years later. Someone moved a body — or created one. Emotional beat: the machinery of the lie laid bare, brick by brick.

chapters.title: The Night Before Dinner
chapters.summary: POV Maren and Casper, alternating. Maren agrees to come to the dinner if Casper guarantees her exit; Casper receives a note: 'One of us confesses tomorrow. Choose which.' Julian's driver is seen buying rope. Emotional beat: dread tightening like a noose; everyone has chosen their role.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Under crystal and candlelight, Casper publicly reads Aldous's confession and the trust ledgers. Julian, cornered, drops the charm and threatens the room with what the parish owes him — and reaches for Maren. Emotional beat: the mask shattering; the whole town as witness.

chapters.title: The Witness Stands
chapters.summary: POV Maren. Maren rises and names her sister, herself, and what she saw on the cliff path. Julian breaks, confessing the accidental fall and the forty-year cover-up his father built to protect the trust — and him. Emotional beat: catharsis; loyalty finally kneeling before truth.

chapters.title: Requiem, Sung at Last
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Weeks later, the trust is restored, the crypt opened, and Lila Voss's name read aloud at a memorial where Maren plays the restored organ. Casper's final episode ends not with a verdict but with the music. Emotional beat: mourning becoming memory — the parish, late, finally arrives.
